guard.notes: .zcode/config.json sets hooks.enabled=true and registers a PreToolUse hook (matcher Bash|Write|Edit|Read|Grep|Glob) that runs the guard with AGENT_RUNTIME=zcode and AGENT_RUNTIME_CONFIG=.agents/runtime/zcode/config.json via ${ZCODE_PROJECT_DIR} paths; exit 0 allows, exit 2 blocks. The policy engine is .agents/runtime/guard.mjs, local to this repository.

capabilitiesNotes: toolEvents: this file's own guard.notes already record the confirmed fact - "No vendor adapter exists in the repository ... There is no project hook, so the policy in tooling/agentos/agent-hooks is honoured behaviourally" - no PreToolUse mechanism exists in this repository for ZCode, matching hooksSupport: behavioral. The other five: no script, doc or event log here has ever exercised a ZCode subagent, resume, cancel, usage report or worktree-aware run, and even the model table below is unverified - left unknown rather than assumed. Updated 2026-09-30: .zcode/config.json now wires a native PreToolUse hook to the local guard, so toolEvents moves to `unknown` - `verified` at the first exercised run in this repository.

permissions.notes: Reads and writes go through the host's own permission prompt; shell runs in its sandbox on top of the guard policy. Structural changes to roles, agents or skills, destructive actions and releases always need explicit user approval, in every mode.
